label: Why Weak Solutions Are Secretly Smooth
notes: Appendix B answers a foundational worry: moduli spaces are built from weak analytic objects, yet the curves must end up smooth. The plan threads Sobolev spaces, the Calderon-Zygmund estimate, Laplace regularity, and bootstrapping into one machine that upgrades a weak solution to a genuinely smooth pseudoholomorphic curve.

label: Sobolev Spaces and Weak Derivatives
notes: A weak derivative is a promise that integration by parts holds against every compactly supported test function, not a new pointwise formula. The space W to the k,p collects functions whose weak derivatives through order k lie in L-p, giving us a Banach completion where the analysis of curves can safely happen.

label: Sobolev Embedding: Decay Buys Continuity
notes: Embedding theorems trade Sobolev regularity for pointwise control. Once kp exceeds the dimension n, functions in W to the k,p are continuous, even Holder continuous. In the Fourier model the membership condition is tail decay: each extra derivative weights coefficients by frequency, so faster decay purchases more classical smoothness for free.

label: Elliptic Operators and Their Symbols
notes: An operator is elliptic when its principal symbol is invertible away from zero frequency. The Laplacian has symbol the squared length of xi, and the Cauchy-Riemann operator dbar has symbol linear and nonzero off the origin. Ellipticity is exactly the algebraic condition that lets us invert and gain derivatives.

label: The Fundamental Elliptic Estimate
notes: The a priori estimate is the engine of the whole appendix. It bounds the full W to the k plus one, p norm of u by the operator output Du in W to the k,p plus a harmless lower-order L-p term. Every derivative of u is controlled by what the elliptic operator produces.

label: Calderon-Zygmund for the Hessian
notes: Solving minus Laplacian u equals f gives second-derivative multipliers xi-i xi-j over the squared length of xi. These are order-zero, bounded symbols, not order-two ones. For p equal to two the Hessian identity is exact; for general p the singular-integral Calderon-Zygmund theory supplies the bound that controls every second derivative.

label: Calderon-Zygmund for dbar
notes: For the Cauchy-Riemann operator the same philosophy yields the basic estimate: the full W to the one,p norm of u is bounded by the L-p norm of dbar u plus a lower-order term. This first-order Calderon-Zygmund inequality is what makes the pseudoholomorphic curve equation elliptic and tractable.

label: Laplace Regularity: Gaining Two Derivatives
notes: Interior regularity localizes with a cutoff, compares against the fundamental-solution convolution, and absorbs the harmonic remainder via Weyl's lemma. A weak solution of a Laplace equation inherits two more derivatives than its right-hand side. In Fourier terms the inverse Laplacian divides every nonzero mode by the squared frequency.

label: Bootstrapping: Climbing the Sobolev Ladder
notes: Bootstrapping iterates the elliptic estimate. A weak solution in W to the one,p has data forcing one more derivative, landing it in W to the two,p; rerun and reach W to the three,p, and so on. With smooth coefficients the climb never stalls, so the solution is infinitely differentiable, hence smooth.

label: The Exponent Ladder for the Product Term
notes: The delicate step is the product of dJ and du. If both sit only in L-p the product can fall to L-p-over-two. Holder gives a source in L-r with one over r equal to one over p plus one over q; improving q by Sobolev embedding lifts r past two, where continuity returns the product to L-p.

label: Application: J-holomorphic Curves Are Smooth
notes: For an almost complex structure J of class C-infinity, any W to the one,p solution of the dbar-J equation with p above two is smooth. The dependency chain runs from the weak curve through coordinates, the Laplace form, Calderon-Zygmund, interior regularity, the embedding threshold, and the finite ladder to a smooth curve.

label: Recap: The Regularity Machine
notes: Four layers compose into one upgrade. Sobolev spaces stage weak derivatives, Calderon-Zygmund tames second derivatives through the Laplacian, Laplace regularity adds two derivatives locally, and bootstrapping iterates the gain. The geometric payoff is decisive: weak pseudoholomorphic curves are as smooth as the almost complex structure allows.
